record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: In what sense does a Regge spacetime, modeled as a piecewise linear manifold with piecewise linear metric data, approximate a smooth vacuum spacetime, and what analogous convergence statement holds for numerical-relativity spacetimes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g)=0$. A Regge spacetime is a four-dimensional piecewise linear manifold $(K,\ell)$ obtained by gluing flat Lorentzian 4-simplices along their tetrahedral faces, where the geometry is specified entirely by the assignment $\ell$ of squared edge lengths to the 1-simplices of $K$; curvature is concentrated as conical defects (deficit angles) on the 2-simplices ("bones"), and the Regge equations of motion are obtained by varying the Regge action $S_R(K,\ell)=\tfrac{1}{8\pi G}\sum_{\sigma^2}A(\sigma^2)\,\varepsilon(\sigma^2)$, where $A(\sigma^2)$ is the area of the bone $\sigma^2$ and $\varepsilon(\sigma^2)$ its deficit angle.

(a) Formulate and prove a precise sense in which a sequence $\{(K_n,\ell_n)\}_{n\ge 1}$ of Regge spacetimes satisfying the Regge equations of motion converges, as the simplicial refinement is increased (e.g., the maximal edge length tends to zero, subject to suitable non-degeneracy/fatness conditions on the simplices), to a smooth solution $(M,g)$ of the vacuum Einstein equations. Specify in what topology or measure-theoretic sense the discrete metric data $\ell_n$, the associated curvature distributions, and the Regge action approximate $g$, the Riemann/Ricci tensor of $g$, and the Einstein–Hilbert action of $g$.

(b) Formulate and prove an analogous convergence statement for spacetimes produced by numerical relativity: given a convergent family of numerical solutions to a well-posed formulation of the Einstein evolution equations on a sequence of grids with resolution tending to zero, identify the appropriate function-space topology and norms in which the numerical spacetimes approach a smooth (or suitably regular) vacuum solution, together with explicit convergence rates.
artifact.category_tag: Regge calculus and numerical relativity convergence
artifact.status_search_result: Several partial results are known: Cheeger–Müller–Schrader proved that the Regge action and curvature converge in the sense of measures to their continuum counterparts under fatness conditions on the simplices; Barrett established a convergence criterion in the linearized regime; and more recent works (e.g., on the definition of curvature in Regge calculus, 2024) refine these. A fully general convergence theorem for nonlinear vacuum Regge solutions to smooth Einstein vacuum solutions, and a comparably general statement for numerical-relativity spacetimes, does not appear to be established.

status_evidence.title: On the definition of curvature in Regge calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Curvature convergence results for Regge metrics in the sense of measures, building on Cheeger–Müller–Schrader.
status_evidence.claim: Partial convergence results (measure-theoretic) for Regge curvature toward smooth curvature are known.

status_evidence.title: On the linearization of Regge calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Barrett's convergence criterion in the linearized case for solutions of the Regge equations relative to Einstein's equation.
status_evidence.claim: Linearized convergence of Regge solutions to smooth Einstein solutions has been formulated.

status_evidence.title: Regge calculus - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of Regge calculus and discussion of piecewise-linear approximation of smooth manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: The convergence of Regge spacetimes to smooth spacetimes is treated as a limiting process in piecewise-linear approximations.
